reports.title: OPEC+ Decides 2027: A Capacity Audit, an Iraqi Revolt and a Glut on the Horizon
reports.summary: OPEC+ ministers meet online on Sunday 29 November to set output for 2027, with no agreed framework beyond 31 December and the first independent audit of members’ capacity on the table.

reports.title: Too Big to Smuggle: Nvidia’s Most Restricted Racks Turn Up in Shanghai, Pledged as Loan Collateral
reports.summary: Chinese loan filings reviewed by Bloomberg show a GB300 NVL72 rack, 72 of Nvidia’s most advanced chips, installed at a Shanghai data centre linked to Alice Huang and pledged to secure a ¥96 million bank loan.

reports.title: The Four-Day Comeback: Wall Street’s Best Week Since April 2025, Inside Its Worst November Since 2008
reports.summary: The S&P 500 rose 5.6% in a holiday-shortened week, the Dow had its biggest weekly gain since October 2022 and the VIX fell by about a third, as Nvidia’s reinstatement of Jensen Huang set off a squeeze in AI shares.

reports.title: Cut Off and Propped Up: Washington Closes China’s Cloud Loophole as Beijing Rescues Its Chip Stocks
reports.summary: Nvidia has told Dell and Supermicro to stop shipping AI servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, according to the Financial Times, after a US rule made those countries licence destinations on 19 November.

reports.title: Europe’s Second Inflation Shock: 4% Prices, a Third ECB Hike and France as the New Periphery, With What It Means for Spain
reports.summary: Euro-area inflation has more than doubled this year to 4.0%, the highest since 2023, driven by energy prices up 21% after the Iran war.

reports.title: Why US Inflation Will Not Come Down: Three Shocks, Sticky Services and a Fed Barely Above Neutral
reports.summary: US inflation has risen from about 2.5% early this year to 3.6% on the Fed’s preferred measure, and core prices have risen 0.3% a month for three months.

reports.title: The $1 Trillion Day: Huang’s Return Sparks the Biggest Rebound Since April 2025
reports.summary: After seven straight losses and a correction, US stocks staged their strongest rebound in 19 months on Monday.

reports.summary: Anthropic opened on Nasdaq at $111.50, 34% above its $83 IPO price, touched $115.10 and a valuation near $2 trillion, then closed at $97.17, up 17.1%, worth about $1.76 trillion fully diluted and the seventh most…

reports.summary: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share on Wednesday evening, above its $70-78 marketed range, and increased the size of the offering, according to Bloomberg and CNBC.

reports.summary: Days before Nvidia’s results, SemiAnalysis, one of the most closely followed independent semiconductor research firms, cut its forecast for global AI accelerator spending in 2028 by 28% to $758 billion and in 2029-30…

reports.summary: Asian chip markets slumped on Monday as Taiwan’s Taiex lost 6.03%, its second-largest points fall on record, and Korea’s Kospi 3.59%, with $3.1 billion of foreign selling across the two.

reports.summary: In his first visit to a regional Fed bank as chair, Kevin Warsh opened the Fed’s productivity and jobs conference in San Francisco by casting AI, which he calls ‘super intelligence’, as possibly the most…

reports.summary: In its IPO roadshow, Anthropic said its Claude Mythos Preview model brought up one Claude model’s prompt processing on AMD MI355X chips in about three days, writing or porting almost all the kernels with little human…

reports.title: Bitcoin Below $67,000: ETF Outflows, a Hawkish Fed and Strategy’s Index Exit
reports.summary: Bitcoin fell below $67,000 on Saturday, its lowest since August, down about 12% this week and 47% below its October 2025 peak, even as US stocks had their best week since August.

reports.title: Back Above 5%: Why the 10-Year Treasury Yield Is Rising Again and What It Means
reports.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield climbed back above 5% this week, reaching 5.17% on Friday, after the October CPI showed a third hot month for core inflation and Fed officials signalled more hikes.

reports.title: SpaceX and Tesla Edge Towards a $3.5 Trillion Merger: What the Largest Deal Ever Would Mean
reports.summary: Bloomberg reported on 12 November that SpaceX and Tesla are making progress in merger talks and could announce a deal as soon as December, or early 2027.

reports.title: The End of the Jensen Era: Huang Resigns, Kress Steps In and Nvidia Searches for Its Second CEO
reports.summary: Jensen Huang resigned on 12 November as president, chief executive and director of Nvidia, the company he co-founded in 1993 and led to become the centre of the AI economy.

reports.summary: On 11 November The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang had a relationship with Kimberly Powell, an Nvidia vice-president who reports to him, days after he admitted an affair with a woman US intelligence suspects…

reports.summary: CoreWeave, the largest specialised AI cloud, beat estimates and raised its 2026 guidance on 10 November: revenue rose 168% to $3.66 billion, its backlog reached $132.5 billion and adjusted operating margins turned…

reports.title: Claude Fable 5.2: The Benchmarks, the Price Cut and What It Means for the AI Trade
reports.summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 on 9 November, the same underlying model with and without its strongest cyber and biology safeguards.

reports.title: Nvidia’s Founder Under Investigation: What the Jensen Huang Affair Means for the World’s Most Important AI Company
reports.summary: Special report. Nvidia’s board has opened an independent investigation after reports about its chief executive. What is reported, what is confirmed, and the governance and policy risks for the company.

reports.title: 48 Hours to the Rare-Earth Deadline: What Revives on 11 November Unless Beijing Signs
reports.summary: The truce runs to 10 January 2027 in politics, but China’s legal suspension of its rare-earth controls still expires on 10 November, as do 178 US tariff exclusions. What revives unless new notices appear.

reports.title: Berkshire’s Favourite Stock Is Berkshire: A Record Buyback, a Bigger Cash Pile and a Weaker GEICO
reports.summary: Greg Abel’s Berkshire spent a record $9.6 billion on buybacks in the third quarter and was a small net seller of other stocks. Operating earnings fell 5.8% as insurance underwriting dropped 43%.

reports.title: Jobs Blowout: 165,000 Payrolls Put the December Hike Back in Play
reports.summary: October payrolls rose 165,000, almost three times consensus, and unemployment fell to 4.1%. Yields and the dollar rose and markets lifted the odds of a December Fed hike to about 77% to 80%.

reports.title: The Fortress in a Falling Market: Berkshire Reports With $365 Billion and a Record Stock
reports.summary: Berkshire reports on 7 November after the worst day for US stocks since April 2025, with its shares near a record. What to watch, why the stock acts as a haven and how Greg Abel has started spending the cash.

reports.title: Six Minutes, $2 Trillion: The Day the AI Trade Cracked
reports.summary: Long-form research. The S&P 500 lost more than $2 trillion and the chip index more than 10% in a day. The sell-off reconstructed, the three forces behind it, the historical context and what comes next.

reports.title: The Data-Centre Backlash: How the Midterms Hit the AI Build-Out
reports.summary: Long-form research. 38 of 39 counted local ballot measures restricted data centres, and power stocks fell up to 23% the next day. The backlash, the electricity bills behind it and what it means for the AI trade.

reports.title: Jobs Friday Preview: What October’s Payrolls Mean for the Fed
reports.summary: The last jobs report before the Fed’s 9 December meeting. Consensus expects about 65,000 jobs and 4.2% unemployment. The trend, the revisions, the forecasts and how markets could react to each outcome.

reports.title: Palantir Q3 2026: The Best Quarter in Its History, and Why the Stock Fell
reports.summary: Long-form research. Revenue up 96% to $2.31 billion and guidance raised to 91% growth, yet the shares fell after hours. The quarter by segment, the pipeline, the valuation debate and what it says about AI demand.

reports.title: Inside Anthropic’s S-1: The Numbers Behind the Largest AI IPO
reports.summary: Long-form research. Anthropic’s prospectus read for investors: $33.2 billion of revenue in nine months, a first operating profit, nearly $900 billion of committed spending and the Long-Term Benefit Trust.

reports.title: Midterms 2026: The Election-Day Guide for Investors
reports.summary: What is at stake, what prediction markets price, the races that decide the Senate, what to watch hour by hour on election night, what history says and how each outcome could affect sectors. It takes no position.

reports.title: The Charts That Explain 2026
reports.summary: Long-form research. The story of the markets in 2026 in twelve chapters, from the oil shock and the return of inflation to the AI build-out, the crypto bear market and Japan's exit from deflation.

reports.title: Oil Shocks Compared: 2026 Against 1973, 1979, 1990 and 2022
reports.summary: Long-form research. Each major oil shock since 1970 reconstructed from the data: what happened to inflation, rates, jobs and stocks in the three years that followed, and how much of that history applies now.

reports.title: Japan Hits 2%: The End of a 30-Year Fight Against Deflation
reports.summary: The Bank of Japan said for the first time that underlying inflation is consistent with its 2% target and signalled a hike as soon as December. What it declared, how Japan got here, and what it means for the yen.

reports.title: The Neocloud Squeeze: When Lenders Stop Funding the AI Build-Out
reports.summary: The GPU cloud companies have lost a third of their market value in a month and, by several accounts, access to the bond market. The business model, the numbers, who is exposed and what it means for the AI trade.

reports.title: Bonds and Gold: When Safe Havens Stop Agreeing
reports.summary: The 10-year yield touched 5.31%, its highest since 2002, then fell; gold dropped below $3,900 from about $5,000. Why the usual hedge behaved like a rate-sensitive asset, and what the curve is saying.

reports.title: NVIDIA Into 17 November: The $108 Billion Quarter
reports.summary: NVIDIA reports on 17 November after guiding to $108 billion of revenue, more than twice a year earlier. What it guided, what consensus expects, the lines that matter and how the backdrop has changed.

reports.title: Binance, Update: $6.3 Billion, North Korea and the Bill
reports.summary: Binance confirmed that about $6.3 billion was stolen from its hot wallets, four times the previous record, in an attack attributed to North Korea. Confirmed figures replace the estimates in report 2026-72.

reports.title: Big Oil’s Windfall Quarter: Exxon and Chevron at Record Highs
reports.summary: Exxon earned $15.4 billion and set $20 billion of 2027 buybacks; Chevron’s profit nearly tripled. Where the money came from, what they do with it and what it says about the oil market.

reports.title: Inflation Is Back: The Fed, the ECB and the BoJ at a Crossroads
reports.summary: US PCE inflation at 3.6%, a split Fed, an ECB losing Lagarde early and a Bank of Japan at its 2% target. Where each central bank stands, what markets price and what to watch into December.

reports.title: Tech’s Worst Day Since June: Intel, Chips and the AI Payoff Question
reports.summary: Intel fell 29% on a weak guide, the chip index lost 7.2% and the Nasdaq 2.9%. What moved, why it spread across the chain and what it says about where the AI cycle stands.

reports.title: The Truce That Isn’t on Paper: US-China After 10 November
reports.summary: The US-China truce is extended in politics to 10 January, but its legal texts still expire on 9 and 10 November. What lapses, how tariffs and trade have shifted, and what is at stake for markets.

reports.title: The $730 Billion Question: Big Tech’s AI Capex and What It Means for Investors
reports.summary: Cloud growth accelerated at Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon, yet the market sold two of them as capex outran cash flow. The results, the funding, the accounting and the scenarios for 2027.

reports.title: The Binance Breach
reports.summary: Billions left Binance hot wallets, issuers froze about $1.8 billion of stablecoins and Bitcoin fell below $79,000. What is confirmed, what is only claimed, and what it means for a market in a bear phase.

reports.title: Midterms 2026: What Markets Are Pricing
reports.summary: Prediction markets and models point to a change in control of at least one chamber on 3 November. What is priced, the Senate races that decide it, what history says and what each outcome means for policy.

reports.title: The US Consumer at the Limit
reports.summary: Sentiment near record lows, gasoline above $4 and real wages falling, yet retailers forecast a first trillion-dollar holiday season. What holds spending up, who carries it and where it could crack.

reports.title: Europe’s Winter Gas Squeeze
reports.summary: TTF crossed €100/MWh for the first time since 2022 with storage at a record low for the season. Prices, storage, the contest with Asia for LNG, policy, exposed industries and the winter outlook.

reports.title: Big Tech’s AI Bill Comes Due
reports.summary: Alphabet, Microsoft and Meta all grew revenue by about a fifth or more in the September quarter, but the market only paid where operating cash covered the spending. The three quarters compared.

reports.title: The Warsh Fed: A Pause, Two Dissents and Fewer Meetings
reports.summary: The Fed held at 3.75% to 4.00% on 28 October with two officials voting to hike, and plans fewer meetings. The decision, inflation and jobs, the bond market, the Warsh agenda and the path into December.

reports.title: Oil Above $115: The Gulf Under Fire
reports.summary: Claimed attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure pushed Brent above $115 with damage still unconfirmed. Hormuz and the bypass routes, the supply balance, gas, inflation, winners and losers, and the scenarios.

reports.title: The United Kingdom: Inflation, Gilts and the Budget
reports.summary: September inflation rose to 3.5%, borrowing ran above forecast and net debt passed £3 trillion in the week before the Budget. Inflation, jobs, the Bank of England, gilts, public finances and the scenarios.

reports.title: Tesla and SpaceX: Anatomy of a $3.4 Trillion Merger
reports.summary: Elon Musk confirmed that Tesla and SpaceX boards have formed committees to study a combination. No terms exist yet. The two businesses, the valuation gap, the governance hurdles and the likely outcomes.

reports.title: The US Deficit: $2 Trillion and the Price of Borrowing
reports.summary: Interest now costs more than defence and the 10-year yields above 5%. The deficit, the cost of interest, the debt, Treasury supply and demand, ratings and the policy options.

reports.title: Russia Sanctions: The Graham Act Waiver and Its Market Consequences
reports.summary: President Trump waived the new sanctions and secondary tariffs two days before they took effect; existing sanctions remain. What was suspended, why oil and diesel drive the decision, and what it means for markets.

reports.title: Anthropic: Growth, Capital and the Road to a Public Listing
reports.summary: Annualised revenue has risen from about $1bn to more than $65bn in nineteen months and the company is preparing to list. What the latest data show and what an IPO valuation would assume.

reports.title: Lockheed Martin: Backlog, Execution and the Arsenal Trade
reports.summary: A record $230bn backlog and a world that is rearming, against costly programme losses and a share price a quarter below its March high. Results, segments, the defence budget and the valuation.

reports.title: Private Credit Under Higher Rates
reports.summary: A US$2 trillion market lending mostly at floating rates to mid-sized, highly leveraged companies, now facing a hiking Fed. Defaults, hidden stress, retail redemptions, contagion channels and the 2007 comparison.

reports.title: The US Housing Market at a 5% Ten-Year Yield
reports.summary: The 30-year mortgage rate has risen from 5.98% in February to 7.40%. Affordability, the lock-in effect, prices, builders, rents, mortgage credit against 2006, policy and the scenarios for 2027.

reports.title: Capital Expenditure, Depreciation and the Quality of US Earnings
reports.summary: AI chips are expensed over five or six years while the chipmaker books the profit at once. How much that timing gap and other AI-era accounting flatter S&P 500 earnings, and when the bill arrives.

reports.title: Financing the AI Build-Out in 2027: The $1.2 Trillion Question
reports.summary: AI infrastructure spending passes $1 trillion next year, more than Big Tech’s own cash covers. Who funds the gap, through which markets, at what cost, and where the risk ends up.

reports.title: EUR/USD: An In-Depth Assessment
reports.summary: The euro is at its lowest against the dollar since May 2025 after four weekly declines. The drivers, from monetary policy and energy to French fiscal stress, tested against the data.

reports.title: USD/CNY: A Quantitative Review
reports.summary: The renminbi is at its strongest against the dollar since mid-2022, in a move tightly managed by the People’s Bank of China. How controlled the trend is and how the central bank is now slowing it.

reports.title: USD/CAD: A Quantitative Review
reports.summary: The dollar is at a one-year high against the Canadian dollar in one of the calmest moves on record. Why oil has stopped helping the loonie, and what the numbers say before the Bank of Canada meets.

reports.title: AUD/USD: A Quantitative Review
reports.summary: The Australian dollar is still up for the year, helped by the most hawkish central bank in the G10, but it has lost almost 4% in a month. The trend break, record-low volatility and the role of risk appetite.

reports.title: USD/CHF: A Quantitative Review
reports.summary: The dollar has gained more than 5% against the Swiss franc this year, making the franc one of the weakest major currencies. How stretched the move is and what could reverse it.

reports.title: GBP/USD: A Quantitative Review
reports.summary: Sterling has slipped to a three-month low while gilt yields hit their highest since 2007. How the pound trades, what drives it and what the numbers imply before the 28 October Budget.

reports.title: USD/JPY: A Quantitative Review
reports.summary: Dollar-yen is back near 158, close to where Tokyo and Washington intervened in July. The trend, volatility, tail risk and drivers of the pair, and what the numbers say about the coming weeks.

reports.title: OpenAI Revenue and the Market
reports.summary: A report that OpenAI’s annualised revenue is about $50 billion, not the $70 billion that circulated a week earlier, hit the stocks most tied to the company. What the reports say and what the gap means.

reports.title: Semiconductors and Rates
reports.summary: Chip stocks have almost doubled this year even as bond yields rose a full percentage point. Earnings have outrun rates so far. The state of the market and what further rate increases could mean for it.

reports.title: ASML
reports.summary: Every advanced chip is printed on an ASML machine. Sales guidance is up about 16% and next year’s EUV capacity is almost sold out, but China and the pace of AI spending make the shares volatile.

reports.title: AMD
reports.summary: Data centre revenue doubled, rack-scale AI systems are shipping and three of the largest AI developers have signed up. The shares have roughly tripled and trade above the average target.

reports.title: Broadcom
reports.summary: The designer of custom AI chips for the largest AI developers says its AI revenue will double next year and again the year after. The shares are still a quarter below their high on fears of competition.

reports.title: TSMC: Semiconductor Series
reports.summary: The world’s chip factory is growing faster than at any time in the past decade, and September sales suggest third-quarter revenue will beat its own guidance. The results, the expansion, the valuation and the risks.

reports.title: Nvidia: Semiconductor Series
reports.summary: Revenue doubled again and the next quarter is guided above $100 billion, yet the shares have risen far less than the chip sector this year. The market is asking how long this can last, not whether demand is real.

reports.title: Wall Street on Rates
reports.summary: After the Fed’s first increase since 2023, the large US banks agree rates will stay high but disagree on how many more hikes are coming. A weak jobs report and yields above 5% make the next step harder to call.

reports.title: JPMorgan Chase: Earnings Preview
reports.summary: The largest US bank reports on 13 October after a record second quarter. Management has guided to strong trading and dealmaking again, but its own executives say the cycle feels almost too good.

reports.title: Amazon
reports.summary: AWS is growing at its fastest pace in four years and earns most of the profit, but AI data centre spending has turned free cash flow negative. Whether the bet pays back.

reports.title: Constellation Brands
reports.summary: Second-quarter results beat expectations, but the beat came from refilling distributor warehouses rather than from more people buying Modelo and Corona. What the numbers say about demand.

reports.title: FOMC Minutes: September Meeting
reports.summary: The Fed raised rates unanimously in September, but the minutes show a committee that agreed on the move far more than on the reasons. Most officials expect one more increase by year end.

reports.title: SpaceX
reports.summary: The largest IPO in history created a $2 trillion company that is three businesses in one: satellite internet, rocket launches and a loss-making AI compute venture. What investors own and what the price assumes.

reports.title: Micron
reports.summary: An 87% gross margin, revenue up almost fivefold in a year and a $1.2 trillion valuation in the strongest memory upcycle on record. The fourth-quarter results and why seven times earnings may still be a cyclical bet.

reports.title: Alphabet
reports.summary: Search still grows, Google Cloud is up 82% and the antitrust cases ended without a break-up. The price is $200 billion of capex a year and the first negative cash flow quarter in two decades.

reports.title: Coca-Cola
reports.summary: One of its best years in a decade, under a new chief executive and with volumes growing again. The business model, the shift from price to volume, the $20 billion tax dispute and the valuation.

reports.title: Novo Nordisk
reports.summary: Europe’s most valuable company invented the modern obesity market, then lost it. How Novo fell from leader to challenger, what the Wegovy pill changes, and whether nine times earnings is value or a trap.

reports.title: Oracle
reports.summary: A software company turned debt-financed builder of AI data centres. The backlog is enormous and half of it is one customer, cash flow is negative and the rating is one notch above junk. Can the bet pay off?

reports.title: Nvidia
reports.summary: The world’s most valuable company is still doubling its revenue. The business, the latest quarter, the financing that now surrounds its customers, and what a $5.6 trillion valuation actually assumes.

reports.title: Paramount and Warner Bros.: Transaction Analysis
reports.summary: The $110 billion takeover that reshapes Hollywood closes on 6 October. How the deal was won, how it is financed, what the regulatory settlement costs, and whether the combined company can carry its debt.
